alpha_high.why: -p 0.5, the top of that range, where nearly every sgRNA is kept.

alpha_low.why: -p 0.05, the bottom of the range crisprFunction.py clamps to. A small alpha keeps few sgRNAs per gene, so goodsgrna counts and the kept-set prefix logic are stressed differently.

control_heterogeneous.why: The control null combined with by-group permutation, so the resampled percentiles are drawn once per sgRNA count. The two features interact and are worth testing together.

control_matched.why: --control with a list that matches real sgRNAs. The null is resampled from control-sgRNA percentiles instead of drawn uniformly, which is a different distribution rather than a different route to the same one. Never previously validated.

heterogeneous.why: The default path on a realistic library: eight distinct sgRNA-per-gene counts means eight separate nulls, each sized by its own stratum. The prototype benchmark never exercised this.

homogeneous_5.why: Baseline. One permutation stratum, the default by-group path, continuous values so no ties. If this case fails nothing else is worth reading.

min_goodsgrna.why: --min-number-goodsgrna excludes genes from FDR adjustment (adjustFDR, RRA.cpp:646), which makes them print FDR as the string NA. The port has to reproduce which rows are NA, not just the numbers in the rows that are not.

min_percentile.why: -P, the lower percentile bound. Nothing in the corpus passed it before, because its default of -1.0 cannot exclude anything: the port's lower bound was therefore unreachable, and every golden recorded so far is consistent with it being wrong. -P 0.01 excludes the strongest sgRNAs -- except at index 0, which ComputeLoValue scores whether or not it is in range (RRA.cpp:500-502), so a gene can end up with a lo-value below 1 and no good sgRNAs at all.

min_percentile_control.why:
-P with --control, so the bound applies to a null resampled from control-sgRNA percentiles rather than a uniform one. The C++ passes minPercentile into ComputePermutationbyNumSG as well as into ProcessGroups (RRA.cpp:306-308), so the bound has to reach the null too.

The bound is 0.08 rather than 0.01 because it was chosen from the data instead of by eye. This case's smallest control percentile is 0.0215, so -P 0.01 excludes nothing a resampled null can draw: the case passed whether or not the null was bounded, which makes it no test of the thing it is named for. 0.08 excludes 14 of the 206 control percentiles, so an unbounded null now shows up as wrong p values.

pathway_duplicate_membership.why: Same shape, but with a sub-name repeated inside the field. The C++ does not deduplicate: it appends the row once per occurrence, so P1,P1 gives P1 the row twice and its sgRNA count is larger than the number of distinct rows in it. Measured against the helper, not assumed.

pathway_memberships.why: The group column as the shipped pathway mode writes it: one row per gene, the field a comma-separated list of every pathway containing that gene, NA for none (pathwayFunc.py:155-162). The C++ splits the field and counts the row in each pathway. Nothing else in the corpus has a comma in that column, which is how the first port of this module came to treat P1,P2 as a group named "P1,P2" -- inventing a pathway and leaving the two real ones a member short each -- and why that went unnoticed.

permutation_ceiling.why: --max-permutation-per-group bounds the null size and so raises the smallest reachable p value. The relationship between that bound and p resolution is asserted in test_rra.py; this case checks the port reproduces the bounded null itself.

pooled_permutation.why: --no-permutation-by-group: one null for all genes regardless of sgRNA count. This is the path the prototype benchmark validated, kept so a regression in it is still caught.

single_sgrna_genes.why: Many genes with exactly one sgRNA. ComputeLoValue always evaluates index 0 before applying the alpha cutoff, so a one-sgRNA gene takes a special path through the kept-set logic.

skip_gene.why: --skip-gene, which crisprFunction.py always passes (as NA/na). Skipped genes bypass permutation, so they exercise a separate branch of the group loop.

tie_extreme.why: Values rounded to whole numbers, which collapses a 300-gene screen onto about a dozen distinct values. Degenerate on purpose: it turns a rare tie-breaking disagreement into one that shows up in almost every gene.

tie_heavy.why: Values rounded to two decimals, so sgRNAs tie by the dozen. Percentiles come from bTreeSearchingF, whose tie resolution depends on the recursion path rather than on a stated rule, so this is where a port most plausibly diverges.

tolerances.note: lo_value and p are printed via %10.4e (five significant figures) and FDR via %f, so the file itself bounds how closely two implementations can be compared.
